phase: W1b: wasm32 error boundaries, and W0's low review follow-ups
change: Core, only under #if arch(wasm32): file- and DAT-supplied values of 2^31 and more are compared in 64 bits before an Int conversion, so wasm32 (a 32-bit Int) reaches the boundary 64-bit hosts reach instead of trapping: BMP file header words 2 and 10 and the palette count (OriginalApplicationStartupInputs), the DIB image size and colour count and the RLE end (OriginalDIBPixels, decoder and validator), a playback file's payload length (OriginalReplayFileInput), the RIFF chunk size (OriginalWaveLoader), the cpoint header frame offset for frame -6 (OriginalWorldCPoints), and a bitmap glyph word for a negative frame, i.e. a player-name byte of 0x80-0xFB (OriginalBitmapDrawing; the reported outOfBounds offset is the word's bit pattern). 64-bit hosts compile the previous lines unchanged. W0 follow-ups: #else instead of early returns in the WASI branches of OriginalConcurrentInputs.Background and OriginalDeferredRelease.retire, the WASI timer counter with &+=, node --disable-warning=ExperimentalWarning and the node version per result row in run_headless_scenarios.py. Tests: OriginalWord32BoundaryTests (6) pin the 64-bit outcomes.
review: Independent review round 1: the fixes correct and 64-bit-equivalent; one missed reachable site, OriginalBitmapDrawing.word: a player name from control.txt or a recording with a byte of 0x80-0xFB gives a negative glyph frame, the word offset wraps past 2^31, 64-bit hosts throw outOfBounds and wasm32 trapped on the first match frame (GBK names; the WASI scenarios use ASCII names). Fixed, with tests; also an RLE test and a stale comment. Scope check of the remaining 197 conversion sites (settings, background loader, catalog, audio backend, network): none file-reachable. Not possible with node:wasi: read-only preopens (the browser runner of W2a mounts /app and /music read-only).
notes: Finding outside this study: such a name is also a boundary (outOfBounds) on 64-bit hosts, because the original reads allocator words in front of the bitmap record for negative frames; rendering non-ASCII names needs that read modelled (core port).
